subject: Sayansi / Science

activities.learning_activity: (a) Explain the concept of science (meaning and branches of science)
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Guide pupils to brainstorm on the meaning of science and its branches
Discussion: Guide pupils to discuss the concept of science
Question and answer: Guide pupils to explain the concept of science by answering questions
Case study: Guide pupils to explain the concept of science through a case study concerning the meaning of science and its branches
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of science is explained correctly
suggested_resources: videos and motion pictures concerning branches of science

activities.learning_activity: (b) Explain human sense organs
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Guide pupils to brainstorm on human sense organs
Discussion: Guide pupils to discuss human sense organs
activities.assessment_criteria: Human sense organs are explained correctly

activities.learning_activity: (a) Identify things found in the environment using sense organs
suggested_methods: Experiments: In groups, guide pupils to conduct investigations using sense organs to identify things found in the environment
activities.assessment_criteria: Things found in the environment are identified correctly using sense organs
suggested_resources: various things in the environment for example: soil, stones, heat source, scent source, sound source, animals, insects, plants and videos of things and living organisms in the environment

activities.learning_activity: (b) Identify living and non-living things
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide pupils in groups to discuss in order to identify features of things and living organisms
Experiments: Guide pupils to conduct experiments to identify things and living organisms
Question and answer: Pupils should be guided to identify living and non-living things through question and answer
activities.assessment_criteria: Living and non-living things are identified correctly
suggested_resources: motion pictures showing characteristics of living things
videos of things and living organisms in the environment
real living organisms and things for example: Insects, animals, plants, stones and soil

activities.learning_activity: (c) Identify main groups of living organisms (plants and animals)
suggested_methods: Question and answer: Pupils should be guided to identify the main groups of living organisms
Investigation: Guide pupils to conduct an investigation in the environment to identify the main groups of living organisms
activities.assessment_criteria: The main groups of living organisms are identified correctly
suggested_resources: Chart with living organisms such as plants, animals and insects

activities.learning_activity: (a) Acknowledge steps of conducting a scientific investigation
suggested_methods: Question and answer: Guide pupils through question and answer to explain the meaning of a scientific investigation
Discussion: Guide pupils to discuss the steps of conducting a scientific investigation
Investigation: Guide pupils to conduct a simple investigation in their environment
activities.assessment_criteria: Steps of conducting a scientific investigation are explained correctly

activities.learning_activity: (b) Conduct simple experiments on living and non-living things
suggested_methods: Experiments: Guide pupils to conduct experiments to identify characteristics and essential needs of living organisms
activities.assessment_criteria: Simple experiments on living and non-living things are conducted correctly

activities.learning_activity: (c) Conserve living organisms in the environment
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Guide pupils to brainstorm on the importance of living organisms in the environment
Discussion: Guide pupils in groups to discuss the importance of living organisms in the environment and ways to conserve them
Gallery walk: Guide pupils to conduct a gallery walk after discussion to learn the importance of living organisms in the environment and ways to conserve them
Project work: Guide pupils to carry out activities to conserve living organisms such as plants and animals
activities.assessment_criteria: Living organisms in the environment are conserved correctly

activities.learning_activity: (a) Use ICT to play simple games that develop the ability to explain scientific events and concepts
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide pupils to discuss procedures for using ICT to play simple games that develop the ability to explain scientific events and concepts
Demonstration: Guide pupils through demonstration to play simple games using ICT
Practical work: Guide pupils to use ICT tools to play games that develop the ability to explain scientific events and concepts
activities.assessment_criteria: ICT is used to play simple games that develop the ability to explain scientific events and concepts

activities.learning_activity: (a) Explaining health principles (balanced diet, physical exercises, personal and environmental hygiene, important signs and information)
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Guide students to brainstorm on the meaning of a balanced diet, physical exercises, personal and environmental hygiene, important signs and information
Discussion: Guide students in groups to discuss the concept of health principles
Guest speaker: Invite a health professional to explain health principles to students
Question and answer: Guide students to explain the concept of health principles
Case study: Guide students to explain the importance of personal and environmental hygiene through a case study
activities.assessment_criteria: Health principles are explained correctly
suggested_resources: Videos, motion pictures of a balanced diet, exercises, personal and environmental hygiene, pictures of important signs, personal hygiene tools, environmental hygiene tools

activities.learning_activity: (b) Explaining major human diseases (modes of transmission, causes, control, and prevention)
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide students to discuss major human diseases
Guest speaker: Invite a health professional to explain to students the types of diseases, modes of transmission, causes, methods of control, and prevention
Case study: Guide students to explain ways to prevent major human diseases through a case study
activities.assessment_criteria: Types of human diseases are elaborated correctly
suggested_resources: Videos and motion pictures of a balanced diet, exercises, personal and environmental hygiene
charts and brochures of various diseases

activities.learning_activity: (c) Explaining the concept of matter (types and properties)
suggested_methods: Question and answer: Guide students through questions and answers to explain the concept of matter
Discussion: Guide students in groups to identify the types and properties of matter
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of matter is explained correctly
suggested_resources: Various objects in solid, liquid, and gas states
pictures and motion pictures of types of matter

activities.learning_activity: (d) Explaining the process of combustion (combustion: meaning, causes, and results)
suggested_methods: Question and answer: Guide students to explain the concept of combustion
Observation: Guide students to observe items that burn so that they can explain the concept of combustion
Discussion: Students in groups should hold discussions to identify the requirements for an object to burn
Experiments: Guide students to conduct experiments on burning objects to explain the concept of combustion
activities.assessment_criteria: The process of combustion is explained correctly
suggested_resources: matchbox or fire lighter and burnable materials such as paper and twigs

activities.learning_activity: (a) Investigating the growth stages of disease-spreading vectors in the environment (e.g., houseflies, cockroaches, and mosquitoes)
suggested_methods: Observation: Guide students to investigate the growth stages of disease-spreading vectors in the environment
Field trip: Guide students to visit areas where vectors are found so that they can identify the growth stages of the vectors
Discussion: Guide students to discuss the growth stages of the vectors they identified as spreading diseases during the field trip
activities.assessment_criteria: Investigation of the growth stages of disease-spreading vectors in the environment is conducted correctly
suggested_resources: housefly, cockroach, mosquito, other vectors found in the environment, and a chart showing vector growth stages

activities.specific_competence: 1.3 Showing understanding of forms of energy and their uses
activities.learning_activity: (a) Acknowledging forms of energy (heat, light, and sound) and their uses
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Guide students to brainstorm on the concept of energy
Observation: Guide students to conduct an investigation of heat, light, and sound energies so that they can explain the concept of energy
Discussion: Guide students in groups to discuss the sources, properties, and uses of heat, light, and sound energies
Demonstration: Guide students to explain various uses of energy through a demonstration
activities.assessment_criteria: Forms of energy and their uses are explained correctly
suggested_resources: videos and motion pictures of heat, light, and sound energy

activities.learning_activity: (a) Performing simple experiments to investigate states of matter
suggested_methods: Case study: Guide students through a case study so that they can identify the states of matter
Experiments: Guide students in groups to perform simple experiments that will enable them to recognize and describe the properties of matter
activities.assessment_criteria: Simple experiments to investigate states of matter are conducted correctly
suggested_resources: Objects in solid, liquid, and gas states

activities.learning_activity: (b) Performing simple experiments to determine the importance of air in combustion
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide students in groups to discuss the importance of air in combustion
Experiments: Guide students in groups to perform simple experiments that will enable them to determine the importance of air in combustion
activities.assessment_criteria: Simple experiments to determine the importance of air in combustion are conducted correctly

activities.learning_activity: (c) Performing simple experiments regarding heat, light, and sound energy
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide students to hold discussions on how to perform simple experiments related to energy
Experiments: Guide students in groups to perform simple experiments related to energy
activities.assessment_criteria: Simple energy experiments are conducted correctly

activities.learning_activity: (a) Using ICT to draw and arrange various shapes logically
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide students to discuss procedures for using ICT to draw and arrange various shapes
Demonstration: Guide students to be able to use ICT to draw and arrange various shapes using a demonstration
activities.assessment_criteria: ICT is used correctly to draw and arrange various shapes
suggested_resources: simple drawing and shape arrangement software

activities.learning_activity: (a) Using a tool that simulates computer programming language (block-based programming languages) to create simple games using a single shape
suggested_methods: Project work: Guide students to create simple games using shapes through a tool that simulates computer programming language
Demonstration: Guide students to figure out how to create simple games using a tool that simulates computer programming language through a demonstration
activities.assessment_criteria: The correct tool simulating computer programming language has been used to create simple games using a single shape.

activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an understanding of scientific theories
activities.learning_activity: (a) Explain the human digestive system (meaning, parts, and their functions)
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Students should be guided to brainstorm on the meaning of digestion
Discussion: Students should be guided to discuss the parts of the human digestive system and their importance
ICT-based learning: Students should be guided to explain the digestive system using a simulation
activities.assessment_criteria: The human digestive system has been explained correctly
suggested_resources: Models/replicas of the human digestive system, and animated videos of the human digestive system

activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an understanding of scientific theories
activities.learning_activity: (b) Explain human reproductive systems
suggested_methods: Discussion: Students in groups should be guided to discuss and explain human reproductive systems
ICT-based learning: Students should be guided to explain the female and male reproductive systems using a simulation
activities.assessment_criteria: Human reproductive systems have been explained correctly
suggested_resources: computer games, videos, and pictures of the human reproductive system

activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an understanding of scientific theories
activities.learning_activity: (c) Explain growth in animals and plants
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Students should be guided to brainstorm on the concept of growth
Discussion: Students in groups should be guided to discuss and explain the concept of growth in animals and plants
activities.assessment_criteria: Growth in animals and plants has been explained correctly
suggested_resources: Models, animated videos, videos, pictures showing growth in animals and plants, and a science set

activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an understanding of scientific theories
activities.learning_activity: (d) Explain the developmental stages of the human body
suggested_methods: Discussion: Students in groups should be guided to discuss and explain the developmental stages of the human body
Question and answer: Students should be guided to explain the developmental stages of the human body through questions and answers
activities.assessment_criteria: The developmental stages of the human body have been explained correctly
suggested_resources: Animated videos, videos, pictures, charts/brochures concerning the developmental stages of the human body

activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Demonstrate an understanding of types of energy and their uses
activities.learning_activity: (a) Explain the concept of magnetism (meaning, properties, and uses)
suggested_methods: Question and answer: Students should be guided to explain the meaning, properties, and uses of magnets using questions and answers
ICT-based learning: Students should be guided to explain the properties and uses of magnets using videos
Discussion: In groups, guide students to discuss and classify the various uses of magnets
Gallery walk: Guide students to conduct a gallery walk after the discussion to learn the various uses of magnets from their peers
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of magnetism has been explained correctly
suggested_resources: Magnets, animated videos, videos explaining the concept of magnetism, a science set, and metallic objects

activities.learning_activity: (a) Perform simple experiments on growth in animals and plants
suggested_methods: Question and answer: Students should be guided to explain the steps for conducting simple scientific experiments through questions and answers
Experiments: Students should be guided to conduct simple experiments on the growth of animals and plants
activities.assessment_criteria: Simple experiments on growth in animals and plants have been performed correctly
suggested_resources: Science set, small animals, animated videos, videos, pictures and charts showing stages of animal and plant growth, plant seeds, and a tape measure or ruler

activities.learning_activity: (b) Perform simple experiments to determine the properties of magnets
suggested_methods: Experiments: Students should be guided in groups to perform simple experiments to determine the properties of magnets
activities.assessment_criteria: Simple experiments to determine the properties of magnets have been performed completely
suggested_resources: Magnets, animated videos, videos showing the properties of magnets, a science set, and metallic objects

activities.learning_activity: (a) Use block-based programming languages to create simple games connecting two shapes
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide students to discuss creating simple games connecting two shapes
Demonstration: Guide students through demonstration on how to use block-based programming languages to create simple games connecting two shapes
Practical tasks: Guide students to use block-based programming languages to create simple games connecting two shapes
activities.assessment_criteria: The appropriate block-based programming tool has been used to create simple games connecting two shapes
suggested_resources: Computers, computer software, and a projector

activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Show an understanding of scientific theories
activities.learning_activity: (a) Explain the respiratory system in animals and plants (meaning, parts of the system and how respiration takes place)
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Guide pupils to brainstorm on the meaning of the respiratory system
Discussion: Guide pupils to discuss the parts of the human and plant respiratory system and how it takes place
ICT-based learning: Guide pupils to explain how the respiratory system works through simulation
activities.assessment_criteria: The respiratory system in animals and plants is correctly explained
suggested_resources: Pictures, charts, and a model of the respiratory system

activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Show an understanding of scientific theories
activities.learning_activity: (b) Explain the concept of acids and bases (meaning, properties, sources and uses)
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide pupils to discuss the meaning, sources, properties and uses of acids and bases
Practical tasks: Guide pupils to perform practical tasks so that they can explain the properties of acids and bases
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of acids and bases is correctly explained
suggested_resources: Real objects containing acids or bases and litmus papers

activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Show an understanding of scientific theories
activities.learning_activity: (c) Explain the concept of machines (meaning, types and uses)
suggested_methods: Question and answer: Guide pupils through question and answer to explain the meaning of a machine
Discussion: Guide pupils in groups to discuss the types and uses of machines
Field trip: Guide pupils to visit places that use machines to produce goods so that they can explain the concept of a machine
Practical tasks: Guide pupils to use simple machines to be able to explain the various uses of machines
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of machines is fluently explained

activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Show an understanding of scientific theories
activities.learning_activity: (d) Explain the concept of floating and sinking
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide pupils in groups to have a discussion on the concept of floating and sinking
Question and answer: Guide pupils to identify the characteristics of objects that can sink and float
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of floating and sinking is correctly explained
suggested_resources: Real objects such as water, a piece of wood and a coin

activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Show an understanding of types of energy and its uses
activities.learning_activity: (a) Explain the concept of electricity (meaning, sources and uses)
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide pupils in groups to discuss the meaning, sources and uses of electricity
Gallery walk: Guide pupils to identify sources of electricity using a gallery walk
Brainstorming: Guide pupils to brainstorm on the uses of electricity and its safety rules
Question and answer: Guide pupils to explain the uses of electricity and its safety rules
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of electricity is correctly explained
suggested_resources: Wires, bulbs, switches, ammeters, voltmeters and batteries

activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Show an understanding of types of energy and its uses
activities.learning_activity: (b) Explain a simple electrical circuit (parts, types, symbols and connection)
suggested_methods: Question and answer: Guide pupils to explain the meaning of a simple electrical circuit through question and answer
Discussion: Guide pupils to discuss the parts, types, symbols and connection of a simple electrical circuit
Demonstration: Guide pupils to explain the parts, types, symbols and connection of a simple electrical circuit through demonstration
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of a simple electrical circuit is correctly explained
suggested_resources: Wires, bulbs, switches, ammeters, voltmeters and batteries

activities.learning_activity: (a) Perform simple experiments to identify acidic or basic substances in the environment
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Guide pupils to brainstorm on various sources of acids in the environment
Experiments: Guide pupils to identify the presence of acids or bases in various objects found in the environment
activities.assessment_criteria: Experiments to identify acidic or basic substances in the environment are correctly performed
suggested_resources: Real objects containing acids or bases and litmus papers

activities.learning_activity: (b) Perform simple experiments concerning machines
suggested_methods: Experiments: Guide pupils to perform various simple experiments using machines
Project work: Guide pupils to construct simple machines
activities.assessment_criteria: Simple experiments concerning machines are correctly performed
suggested_resources: Real objects, simple and complex machines

activities.learning_activity: (c) Perform simple experiments concerning floating and sinking
suggested_methods: Experiments: Guide pupils to perform experiments to identify objects that float and sink
Field trip: Guide pupils to visit lake shore or sea coastal areas to identify how water transport vessels float
Practical tasks: Guide pupils to make models of objects that float or sink
activities.assessment_criteria: Simple experiments on floating and sinking are effectively performed
suggested_resources: Real objects such as water, a piece of wood, a coin, an inflated balloon and pictures of sinking/floating objects

activities.learning_activity: (d) Perform experiments concerning simple electrical circuits
suggested_methods: Project work: Guide pupils to construct a simple electrical circuit
Practical tasks: Guide pupils to perform activities to identify the structure of a simple electrical circuit
activities.assessment_criteria: Experiments on constructing a simple electrical circuit are correctly performed
suggested_resources: Batteries, electrical wires, bulbs and switches

activities.learning_activity: (a) Use a tool simulating computer language (block-based programming languages) to create simple games combining more than two shapes
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide pupils to discuss the use of a simulation tool to play simple games that develop the ability to explain events and scientific concepts
Demonstration: Guide pupils through demonstration to create simple games combining more than two shapes
Experiments: Guide pupils to create simple games combining more than two shapes using a tool simulating computer language (block-based programming languages)
activities.assessment_criteria: The appropriate computer language simulation tool has been used to create simple games combining more than two shapes
suggested_resources: ICT equipment such as computers and projectors, and computer software
